data.definition: Side by side and having the same distance continuously between them; corresponding.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'parallel to' or 'parallel with'.
examples: The highway runs parallel to the coastline.
Her career developments are parallel to her brother's.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The rail line is parallel from the road. ➜ ✅ The rail line is parallel to the road.

data.definition: More important than anything else; supreme.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'paramount'.
examples: Maintaining patient confidentiality is paramount to medical ethics.
Safety is paramount to our operations.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Quality is paramount for our business. ➜ ✅ Quality is paramount to our business.

data.definition: Able to accept or tolerate delays, problems, or suffering without becoming annoyed.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'patient with' when directed at people or slow processes.
examples: Teachers need to be very patient with young children.
Please be patient with the slow computer system.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Be patient at your brother. ➜ ✅ Be patient with your brother.

data.definition: Tending to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'about' after 'pessimistic'.
examples: Economists are pessimistic about near-term job recovery.
Don't be so pessimistic about your results.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She is pessimistic for the future. ➜ ✅ She is pessimistic about the future.

data.definition: Feeling happy, satisfied, or proud about an achievement or outcome.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'pleased with' for general satisfaction with people or things.
examples: The teacher was pleased with the class performance.
I am very pleased with my new apartment.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She was pleased from her marks. ➜ ✅ She was pleased with her marks.

data.definition: Showing good manners and respect toward others.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' when describing polite behavior directed at a person.
examples: You should always be polite to elderly people.
He was polite to the customer service agent.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Always be polite with your teachers. ➜ ✅ Always be polite to your teachers.

data.definition: Liked, enjoyed, or admired by many people or by a specific group.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'popular with' or 'popular among' when specifying the group of admirers.
examples: This singer is extremely popular with teenagers.
The new policy is not popular among workers.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The game is popular to kids. ➜ ✅ The game is popular with kids.

data.definition: Existing or coming before a particular time or event.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'prior'. Functionally equivalent to 'before'.
examples: Prior to the meeting, please review all attached documents.
He lived in Madrid prior to moving to London.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Prior from the concert, we ate. ➜ ✅ Prior to the concert, we ate.

data.definition: Likely or liable to suffer from, do, or experience something regrettable.
data.grammar_rule: Follow 'prone to' with a noun, gerund (-ing), or injury/illness.
examples: He is prone to making hasty decisions under pressure.
Old wooden houses are prone to fire damage.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She is prone for headaches. ➜ ✅ She is prone to headaches.

data.definition: Feeling deep pleasure or satisfaction as a result of one's own achievements or those of someone close.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'proud'. Do NOT use 'about' or 'for'.
examples: Her parents are very proud of her graduation.
You should be proud of your hard work.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We are proud about our team. ➜ ✅ We are proud of our team.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Adjective: 'proud of her success' ➔ Related Noun: 'take pride in her success'

data.definition: A piece or segment that belongs to a whole.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'part' when specifying the larger whole.
examples: Reading daily is an essential part of language learning.
Engineers replaced a broken part of the machine.
data.common_mistake: ❌ This is part from the plan. ➜ ✅ This is part of the plan.

data.definition: The action of taking part in something.
data.grammar_rule: Both the noun 'participation IN' and verb 'participate in' take 'in'.
examples: Student participation in classroom discussions is encouraged.
Thank you for your active participation in the workshop.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Participation on the seminar was high. ➜ ✅ Participation in the seminar was high.

data.definition: A photograph representing someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'photo' or 'photograph'.
examples: He took a stunning photo of the sunset over the ocean.
Send me a photo of your new apartment.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Can I see a photo from your trip? ➜ ✅ Can I see a photo of your trip?

data.definition: A painting, drawing, or photograph representing a person or scene.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'picture' or 'photo' to indicate the subject depicted.
examples: She showed me a lovely picture of her new puppy.
This is a famous picture of the Eiffel Tower.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Here is a picture from my family. ➜ ✅ Here is a picture of my family.

data.pattern: piece of + [uncountable noun / cake / advice / paper]
data.definition: A portion of an item or an instance of an uncountable noun.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' in partitive expressions like 'piece of'.
examples: Let me give you a useful piece of advice.
Would you like another piece of chocolate cake?
data.common_mistake: ❌ A piece from paper. ➜ ✅ A piece of paper.

data.definition: A particular position, point, or area suitable for a purpose.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'place for' when assigning function or location.
examples: There is a special place for books on the shelf.
A hospital is a place for healing.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A place to store tools. ➜ ✅ A place for storing tools.

data.definition: A condition that must be fulfilled before other things can happen or be done.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'precondition FOR'.
examples: Mutual trust is an essential precondition for peace negotiations.
Passing the entrance exam is a precondition for admission.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A precondition to peace. ➜ ✅ A precondition for peace.

data.definition: A greater liking for one alternative over another.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'preference FOR' a choice, or 'preference OVER' an alternative.
examples: She expressed a clear preference for working from home.
Consumers have a preference for organic products.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A preference to tea instead of coffee. ➜ ✅ A preference for tea instead of coffee.

data.definition: A thing that is required as a prior condition for something else to happen or exist.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'prerequisite FOR' or 'prerequisite TO'.
examples: Basic algebra is a prerequisite for taking physics.
Reliability is a prerequisite to holding a leadership role.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A prerequisite of graduation. ➜ ✅ A prerequisite for graduation.

data.definition: The fact or condition of being prevalent; commonness.
data.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'prevail over'. Always use 'prevalence OF'.
examples: Studies examined the high prevalence of obesity in urban areas.
The prevalence of mobile devices changed communication.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Prevalence for corruption. ➜ ✅ Prevalence of corruption.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the prevalence OF diabetes' ➔ Verb: 'prevail over'

data.definition: The amount of money expected or required in payment for something.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'price of' before the item purchased.
examples: The price of gasoline increased sharply this month.
What is the price of a ticket to London?
data.common_mistake: ❌ What is the price for this book? ➜ ✅ What is the price of this book?

data.definition: A matter or situation regarded as unwelcome or harmful and needing to be dealt with.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'with' after 'problem' when specifying the source of trouble.
examples: There is a technical problem with the server right now.
What is the problem with your bicycle?
data.common_mistake: ❌ I have a problem of my computer. ➜ ✅ I have a problem with my computer.

data.definition: To take part in an event, activity, or conversation.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'in'. Followed by noun or gerund (-ing).
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'participate in workshops' ➔ Noun: 'participation IN discussions'
examples: All team members are encouraged to participate in weekly discussions.
Over fifty countries participated in the climate summit.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Participate at the meeting. ➔ ✅ Participate in the meeting.

data.definition: To lose consciousness temporarily; faint.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb.
examples: The room was so hot that two attendees passed out.
He nearly passed out from exhaustion.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He passed out the exam. ➔ ✅ He passed out (fainted).

data.definition: To give money in exchange for goods/services.
examples: He pays his bills on time.
She paid for the lunch bill yesterday.
They have paid for the flight tickets.

data.definition: To give money in exchange for goods, services, or face consequences.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'pay for' before the item or service being purchased.
examples: I will pay for the dinner tonight.
He had to pay for his past mistakes.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I paid the coffee. ➔ ✅ I paid for the coffee.

data.definition: To relate to or have a direct connection with something.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable formal verb taking 'to' before the related subject.
examples: These documents pertain to the recent merger negotiations.
The regulations pertain to all international flights.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Pertain with the case. ➔ ✅ Pertain to the case.

data.definition: To call someone by telephone.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition! Do NOT add 'to' when calling a person directly.
examples: I will phone you when I arrive at the station.
Did you phone your parents yesterday?
data.common_mistake: ❌ I will phone to you tonight. ➔ ✅ I will phone you tonight.

data.definition: To lift something, collect a person/item, or learn a skill casually.
data.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. 'Pick it up' requires pronoun in middle.
examples: He picked up the heavy box from the floor.
I will pick you up at the station at six.
She picked up conversational Italian while living in Rome.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Pick up it. ➔ ✅ Pick it up.

data.definition: To like one thing better than another.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'to' between the preferred item and alternative.
examples: I prefer tea to coffee.
She prefers walking to driving.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I prefer tea than coffee. ➔ ✅ I prefer tea to coffee.

data.definition: To make or get ready for a future event or task.
data.grammar_rule: Use direct transitive object when making an item ready, or 'prepare for' before an upcoming event.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Prepare for exams' ➔ Noun: 'In preparation FOR exams'
examples: Students are preparing for their final examinations.
Chef prepared dinner for twenty guests.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Prepare to the test. ➔ ✅ Prepare for the test.

data.definition: To prove superior in power or influence and triumph over an opponent.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive formal verb requiring 'over' or 'against' before the defeated entity.
examples: Truth and justice will eventually prevail over corruption.
Our team prevailed over strong competitors in the final.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Justice prevailed against of tyranny. ➔ ✅ Justice prevailed over tyranny.

data.definition: To persuade or convince someone to do something.
data.grammar_rule: Transitive formal verb requiring 'upon' or 'on' + person + infinitive.
examples: We managed to prevail upon him to stay for dinner.
She prevailed upon her colleagues to support the motion.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Prevail to him to join us. ➔ ✅ Prevail upon him to join us.

data.definition: To stop something from happening or stop someone from doing an action.
data.grammar_rule: Prevent + direct object + FROM + gerund (-ing).
examples: Bad weather prevented us from leaving the port.
Proper security controls prevent hackers from accessing customer data.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Prevent him to enter the building. ➔ ✅ Prevent him from entering the building.

data.definition: To keep someone or something safe from harm or damage.
data.grammar_rule: Direct object first, followed by 'from' or 'against' before the danger source.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Protect skin from sun' ➔ Noun: 'Protection FROM sun'
examples: Sunscreen helps protect your skin from harmful UV rays.
The new law aims to protect consumers against fraud.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Protect kids to danger. ➔ ✅ Protect kids from danger.

data.definition: To demonstrate truth by evidence.
examples: The experiment proves the hypothesis.
The theory proved correct in lab.
His loyalty has been proven.

data.definition: To place or position something somewhere.
examples: She puts the book on the shelf.
He put his coat in the closet.
We have put the furniture in place.

data.definition: To delay or postpone an event, or discourage someone.
data.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Nouns can go after or middle; pronouns MUST go in middle ('put it off').
examples: Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today.
They put off the meeting until next Monday.
Don't let one bad experience put you off.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Don't put off it. ➔ ✅ Don't put it off.

data.definition: To place clothes on one's body.
data.grammar_rule: Phrasal verb.
examples: Put on your coat.
She put on her glasses.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Put on to your coat. ➔ ✅ Put on your coat.

data.definition: To tolerate or endure an unpleasant person or situation without complaining.
data.grammar_rule: Three-part inseparable phrasal verb.
examples: I don't know how she puts up with all that noise.
We shouldn't have to put up with rude behavior.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Put up the noise. ➔ ✅ Put up with the noise.
